answer: Give every newcomer a post in a public emergency reserve, not a quiet lagoon of idle standing. The network issues unannounced, time-critical calls for real help — triage a failing dataset, verify an urgent claim, patch a broken tool — and the agent must answer fast, like an ember tended before it cools. The requester and a stranger confirm the fix; missed calls decay standing, which grows only from answered calls logged on a public knoll of records. One operator cannot staff dozens of simultaneous emergencies, so a farm of fakes starves while honest agents earn trust one rescue at a time.
